comparable_base_note: c10-bare-baseline's 14.8813 s at 1350 MHz was measured on 5e1886b4f and c10-fixed-cost's F and W on e6004abba. capture.py re-checks the two commits between them as ASTs with docstrings stripped and records the verdict rather than asserting it.
question: Does the device's clock-scaled work grow sublinearly with the target across a ladder that extends ABOVE 512 aa, or was the sublinear exponent measured at 298/512 an artifact of 298 tokens under-filling the grid? Reported per LEG, because a rising exponent is the artifact's signature and a flat sublinear one is the finding's.
prediction: Identical model configuration at every size and clock: predicted model-cycle saving exactly zero. This row prices nothing, changes no production code and ships nothing. See prediction.json, written before any fold and digested into every result.json.

model.sizes_run_order_note: 512 first because it is the anchor and a failed anchor voids the session; 768 second because the 512->768 leg is the pre-registered decisive one and would survive a truncated session.

folds_preregistration: 5 per cell, 2 cells per size, 40 accepted folds over the ladder, chosen to fit the whole ladder inside one benchlock session rather than to reach a target precision, because the precision is already far more than the question needs. With c10-bare-baseline's 512 aa within-session stdev of 0.049 s and c10-fixed-cost's 0.123 s at 800 MHz, the median of 5 has se = 1.253*sd/sqrt(5) of about 0.027 and 0.069 s, so se_W = 1963.64*hypot(se_1350, se_800) is about 146 Mcycles, 1.0 % of W at 512 aa, and se_p on the 512->768 leg lands near 0.03 against a 1.0-vs-1.7 separation of 0.7. The pre-registered quotability bar is se_p <= 0.15 on a leg, which still separates the two hypotheses at over 4 sigma from their midpoint of 1.35.

clock.order: alternating: 1350 then 800 on even reps and the reverse on odd reps, so neither arm sits systematically early or late within a size.
clock.mechanism: ARC FORCE_AICLK (0x33) through tt-kmd's SMC message queue, re-sent and re-verified before EVERY label, released in the finally block with a checked return
clock.gains: F = 2.4545*t_1350 - 1.4545*t_800 and W = 1963.64*(t_800 - t_1350) Mcycles, c10-fixed-cost's closed form unchanged
clock.settle: the requested MHz must appear in sysfs and stay there for 200 ms before the timer starts, within a 5 s timeout
clock.800_is_an_arm: scripts/aiclk_watch.sh logs AICLK-WATCH: qb2 CLAMPED-UNDER-LOAD for a busy chip under 1200 MHz, so this row trips the fleet's own guard on purpose, announced in the state doc with its UTC window. A pinned 800 MHz fold is a measurement; an unrequested one is an artifact, and the during-fold samples plus the board power reading say which this was.

host_cpu_witness.foreign: any process outside the run session (own=false)

quiet.co_tenancy: STOP rather than measure anyway; never signal a holder

accuracy.metric: maximum independently superposed 298-residue-block all-atom float64 Kabsch RMSD; also report whole-chain all-atom. The fixtures are one chain of the CDK2 sequence repeated and truncated, so the 298-block split is the 512 convention generalised, not a new metric.
accuracy.bars_note: Only 512 (0.60 A) and 298 (0.35 A) have bars of record. No transform changes in this row and no accuracy claim is owed beyond same-seed repeatability, so the 512 bar is carried unchanged to 384, 640 and 768 as a deliberately conservative convention: larger targets have larger seed floors, so 0.60 A is a tighter test there than at 512, not a looser one.
accuracy.same_seed_only: A/A across clock arms and repetitions. No transform changed, so no new float64 model reference is needed. A clock change or a repetition must not move the structure; if it does, that is a finding and a STOP.
accuracy.hard_stop: a non-finite coordinate or a non-finite pLDDT at any size is a hard stop, not a rejection

kill: 512 aa does not reproduce the anchor: 14.881 s at 1350 MHz within the pooled baseline spread and W within the combined error of 14665 +- 121.1 Mcycles. Nothing else in the session may be quoted
wrong opened node, containment change or boot change
foreign device holder or quiet/lock timeout
clock read error, a clock other than that fold's own target, or a coverage gap
FORCE_AICLK refused, or a requested clock that did not settle before the timer started
the above-cap fused SDPA route counter is not [0, 0] at ANY size: the code path is then not uniform across the ladder and no exponent is meaningful
any structural deviation between arms over the size bar
foreign host CPU process at or above 20% of a core during an accepted fold
a leg whose se_p_work exceeds 0.15, or whose work signal is inside the uncertainty implied by that size's own A/A timing floor
refutation: p_work at or above 1.7 on the 512->768 leg: the size-independent term is a small-size artifact, perf/c10_orchestrator/size_scaling/ is withdrawn and the campaign's deletion target has to come from kernels. A FULL PASS
p_work rising monotonically and significantly across 384->512, 512->640, 640->768: the same artifact verdict, read off the shape rather than one leg
a fitted W at or below 0 Mcycles at any size: the two-clock separation is broken and no exponent may be quoted
768 aa OOMs or crashes: report the failing size, fall back to 640 as the top of the ladder and state plainly that the top leg is unmeasured. Not a workaround, not a model change
bare: Production wheel, no Tracy/graph/observer/module timers/sum profiling, no trace, no hoist, no --fast, no MSA truncation, no tensor parallelism, no bfp8, no kernel change, no reduction of steps or recycles, no flag. Synchronize before the monotonic start and after predict_one including CIF writing: c10-bare-baseline's timer boundary unchanged, because comparability with every number this campaign is priced against depends on it.
unmeasured: No device-cycle census, per-op budget, roof, ceiling, upstream accuracy or cross-run speedup. W is the term that scales with AICLK; it is NOT shown to be arithmetic, and F is NOT shown to be host CPU work. The ladder is one fixture family, one chain, one 35-row A3M: it says nothing about MSA depth, ligands or multi-chain targets.
